blocks.content: The demo agents carry a name, a version, and labels your charts can break down by. In this milestone you run the Python getting started example, give it its own agent name and version, and replace its hardcoded client tags with one you set from the shell. This milestone happens on your machine. You then find the result in **Agents** and in **Analytics**.
Add a name, a version, and a tag to the sample, then run it.

In a terminal, open the Python getting started example in the `agento11y` repository you cloned in Milestone 3, and set it up the way its `README.md` describes:

```bash
cd agento11y/examples/getting-started/python
cp .env.example .env
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Fill in the values in `.env`, then set one more variable in the shell you will run it from:

```bash
export AGENTO11Y_TAGS=team=learning
```

A client tag is a key-value pair the SDK attaches to every generation, span, and metric it records. On the metrics, this one becomes the label `agento11y_tag_team`.

Open `main.py`. The example hardcodes its client tags, which would override the variable you just set. Comment out line 58:

```python
# tags={"team": "checkout", "env": "dev"},
```

Then, in `GenerationStart`, change the agent name, the version, and the conversation ID:

```python
GenerationStart(
    conversation_id="conv-2",
    agent_name="learning-agent",
    agent_version="1.1.0",
    ...
)
```

The example already declares an agent name and a version. Changing them makes this run a new agent in the catalog, and changing the conversation ID starts a new conversation.

Run the example from that shell:

```bash
python main.py
```

It makes one OpenAI call, so `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be set in `.env`. It prints the response, followed by `Done`.

blocks.checkboxLabel: I commented out the tags, changed the name and version, and ran the example without errors

blocks.content: Your example sent one generation with an agent name, a version, and a tag.
Find the agent in the catalog and the tag on the cost chart.
Go to **Observability** > **Agent** > **Agents** with a time range that covers the last hour.

In **Filter agent by name…**, type `learning-agent`.

The list narrows to your agent. It is no longer anonymous, and its version column reads `1.0.0`, the version you declared, rather than a hash of the prompt.
Go to **Analytics** with the same time range and find the estimated cost chart.

Turn on the chart's breakdown and look at the dimensions it offers. Alongside **Agent**, **Model**, and **Provider**, the label `agento11y_tag_team` is now offered, because your example's metrics carry it. Choose it, and the chart draws one line for `learning`.

Metrics can take a few minutes to arrive. If the label isn't offered yet, wait and reload.

You found your agent in the catalog under the version you declared, and broke a chart down by a label you added. Parents and workflow steps follow the same pattern: your code declares them, and the graphs draw what it declared. The Instrument agent dependencies and workflows page shows the fields.

Don't see `learning-agent`? Check these in order:

1. The example ran from the shell where the `AGENTO11Y_` variables are set, and printed no error.
2. The time range covers the last hour.
3. The agent name in `main.py` is spelled `learning-agent`.

For the reference on what you added, refer to [Understand agent versions](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/agent-observability/observe-and-troubleshoot/agent-catalog/#understand-agent-versions) and [Client tags](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/agent-observability/instrumentation/sdk/#client-tags).
